precepts.text: That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word. The water represents the word of God.
precepts.point: Hear, O Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen. Fear not: I will pour water upon him that is thirsty. Thirsty for what? For the truth.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
The Lord tells Jacob, “Fear not”, and promises, “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty.” Thirsty for what? Thirsty for the truth. Paul shows what that water is: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.” The water represents the word of God.

Read Isaiah with that in mind. “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty”: I will pour the word of God upon them that are thirsty for the truth. “and floods upon the dry ground”: the floods also represent the word of God, poured out on the dry ground, these places wherein we dwell. “I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring”: his spirit upon his people and his blessing upon their children.

God only chose Israel, and this washing is for his chosen, Jacob and Jesurun, “whom I have chosen.” The Lord made us and formed us from the womb, and he will help us.

When the word is poured out, “they shall spring up as among the grass.” That is what we are looking at now: the Israelites are waking up and springing up worldwide like grass. And verse 5 shows three kinds of Israelites waking up: one says “I am the Lord’s”, acknowledging we are the children of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; another takes on a new name and calls himself “by the name of Jacob”; another changes his surname and will “surname himself by the name of Israel.” It is the word of God, the water, that cleanses them and brings them back.

precepts.text: That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure, saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built.
precepts.point: The Lord spoke to a Persian king and he listened, letting us return and build the temple.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
Cyrus the Great founded the Achaemenid Empire, the old Persian kingdom, in 550 BC, and it was an ancient Iranian empire. That makes this very significant for what is going on today. “the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”, and Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem”.

The Lord was working through King Cyrus. The Lord did speak to him, and he listened. Isaiah had already named him: “That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid.”

So the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah was fulfilled through a Persian, an Iranian king, called by God his shepherd, who performed all his pleasure: Jerusalem built again and the foundation of the temple laid.

precepts.text: Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen.
precepts.point: Respect unto His chosen is not respect of persons. Within Israel there is no respect of persons: the Most High renders to every man according to his deeds, tribulation and anguish upon every soul that doeth evil, of the Jew first and also of the Gentile, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom that was Hellenized; but glory, honour, and peace to every man that worketh good. The nation is chosen above the nations, and all Israel shall be saved through the Deliverer out of Sion.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

precepts.why:
Who are the chosen God has respect unto? “Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen”.

Israel is the chosen. So when God looked upon the children of Israel and had respect unto them, he had respect unto his chosen, Jacob his servant, the nation chosen above the nations.

precepts.text: One shall call himself by the name of Jacob, and another surname himself by the name of Israel; the name tells whose people you are.
precepts.point: Reading these family names aloud loosens the tongue to say the names of the scriptures fluently and without hesitation. 1 Chronicles 1 serves the same practice, and it carries the names of Israel's families together with Edom and Ishmael, the nations that come out of Abraham's line.

note.label: Numbers 26: The Second Census of the Families of Israel

precepts.why:
“Hanoch, of whom cometh the family of the Hanochites: of Pallu, the family of the Palluites.” The ending ites means the descendants of, the people you belong to: Israelites are the descendants of Israel, Edomites the descendants of Edom, and so it goes all down the line through the scriptures.

“One shall say, I am the Lord’s; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel.” The name tells whose people you are: one calls himself by the name of Jacob, another surnames himself by the name of Israel, as the Hanochites carried the name of Hanoch.

Reading these family names aloud loosens the tongue to say the names of the scriptures fluently and without hesitation. 1 Chronicles 1 serves the same practice, and it carries the names of Israel's families together with Edom and Ishmael, the nations that come out of Abraham's line.

precepts.text: Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen; the chosen seed the whole passage speaks of.
precepts.point: Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart, that the Lord he is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath; there is none else. Consider is the key word: really appreciate all of it, for Israel could have been born of any nation, but the Most High ordained this people, and the way to cash in is simply keeping the commandments.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen”. This is the chosen seed the whole passage speaks of: “because he loved thy fathers, therefore he chose their seed after them, and brought thee out in his sight with his mighty power out of Egypt”.

He drove out nations greater and mightier than Israel, with more economic might and more military power, but the Most High delivered Israel out of their hands, and to this day the twelve tribes are still here.

“Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart”. Consider is the key word: really appreciate all of it. Israel could have been born of any nation, but the Most High ordained this people, Jacob his servant, Israel whom he has chosen, and the way to cash in is simply keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: The Most High names Cyrus as his shepherd who will say Jerusalem shall be built and the temple foundation laid.
precepts.point: Cyrus was one of the first kings of Persia, and the Most High used him to give the order to rebuild Jerusalem. His coming was prophesied long before by name.

note.label: Ezra 1: Cyrus Stirred Up to Send Israel Home

precepts.why:
Cyrus's coming was prophesied long before, by name. Isaiah says of the Most High, “That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid.”

Here it comes to pass. In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, the Lord stirs up his spirit and he makes a proclamation throughout all his kingdom: “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah.” Cyrus was one of the first kings of Persia, and the Most High named him as His shepherd, the one who would say Jerusalem shall be built and the temple's foundation laid, and used him to give the order to rebuild Jerusalem.

precepts.text: Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen; the servant and witness of the Lord is plainly named Israel.
precepts.point: I, even I, am the Lord, and beside me there is no saviour; I have declared and saved and shown when there was no strange god among you. Before the day was I am he, and there is none that can deliver out of my hand.

note.label: Isaiah 43: Ye Are My Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen”. Who is that servant and witness? Read straight on into the next chapter: “Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen”. The servant and witness of the Lord is plainly named Israel.

This kills the Jehovah’s Witness doctrine, because Jacob is the subject, so the witnesses are Israel. Israel, the blind people that have eyes and the deaf that have ears, is brought forth before all the nations gathered together, and Israel is the witness “that ye may know and believe me, and understand that I am he: before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.” “I, even I, am the Lord; and beside me there is no saviour.”

precepts.why:
“One shall say, I am the Lord’s; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel.” This is prophecy of our name being changed back, and Isaiah 65 shows how it was lost: “And ye shall leave your name for a curse unto my chosen: for the Lord God shall slay thee, and call his servants by another name”.

Ye shall leave your name for a curse unto my chosen, for the Lord shall slay thee and call his servants by another name. Our names were left for a curse in slavery. So when the Most High pours his spirit upon Jacob’s seed and his blessing upon his offspring, they surname themselves by the name of Israel again. On the sabbath classes a member is announced no longer a Corinthian or an Ephesian, because they take a pen and legalize their name change, subscribing with the hand as the scripture said.

Another shall “surname himself by the name of Israel.” Why does the name have to be taken back? Because of the curse: “And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.”

Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb and a byword among all nations. Our nationality and name were changed, called African American, one of the curses driven upon us in the nations whither the Lord led us. Isaiah 44 is the prophecy of the name being changed back: one calling himself by the name of Jacob, another subscribing with his hand unto the Lord, which is why on the sabbath classes a member is announced no longer a Corinthian or an Ephesian, having taken a pen and legalized the name change.

precepts.point: Fear ye not, neither be afraid; have not I told thee from that time and declared it? Ye are even my witnesses. Is there a God beside me? Yea, there is no God, I know not any. Our God stays bragging through the bible that he knows no other God.

note.label: Isaiah 44: The Idol Maker's Folly and the Changed Name

precepts.why:
“I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God.” “Is there a God beside me? yea, there is no God; I know not any.” Our God stays bragging through the bible that he knows no other God, and David tells why: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

All the gods of the nations are idols. They are nothing but stuff our God made, which he gave them to worship, while the Lord, the King of Israel and his redeemer the Lord of hosts, made the heavens. So there is no God beside him, and “ye are even my witnesses” of it: he told it from that time and declared it, since he appointed the ancient people.

That day shall not come except there come a falling away first, and the man of sin be revealed, who exalts himself above all that is called God, sitting in the temple showing himself that he is God. Our people are convinced color does not matter, so it is easy for a white jesus to sit in the temple and show himself to be god, when Christ is shown black from the scripture. “He feedeth on ashes: a deceived heart hath turned him aside”. This is the strong delusion: “Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders, And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.”

His coming is after the working of Satan with lying wonders. Because they received not the love of the truth, which is the law, God sends them strong delusion that they should believe a lie, and all be damned who believe not the truth. That is why “he hath shut their eyes, that they cannot see; and their hearts, that they cannot understand.” Our people are convinced color does not matter, so a white jesus sits in the temple showing himself to be god, when Christ is shown black from the scripture, and the deceived heart cannot say, “Is there not a lie in my right hand?”

precepts.text: Answering whether we must be angry with ourselves for breaking God's laws: godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of, but the sorrow of the world worketh death, so be angry enough to repent and change, not to beat yourself down.
precepts.point: Repentance is for Israel; when he blots out the sins he is speaking of Jacob, the servants that sinned whom God is calling back. Sing O ye heavens, shout ye lower parts of the earth, break forth into singing, for the Lord hath redeemed Jacob and glorified himself in Israel.

note.label: Isaiah 44: The Idol Maker's Folly and the Changed Name

precepts.why:
“I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee.” Repentance is for Israel; when he blots out the sins he is speaking of Jacob, the servants that sinned whom God is calling back. So must we be angry with ourselves for breaking God’s laws? Paul answers: “Now I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance: for ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing. For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.”

Godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of, but the sorrow of the world worketh death. So be angry enough to repent and change, not to beat yourself down. The sorrow that returns you to him is the godly sorrow; then the heavens sing and the lower parts of the earth shout, “for the Lord hath redeemed Jacob, and glorified himself in Israel.”

precepts.point: Now they sin more and more and have made them molten images of their silver, idols according to their own understanding, all of it the work of the craftsmen; they say of them, Let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves. Remember the time frame and the other prophets that were prophesying during that time; the craftsman was making idols in the images of men.

note.label: Hosea 13: In Me Is Thine Help

precepts.why:
“And now they sin more and more, and have made them molten images of their silver, and idols according to their own understanding, all of it the work of the craftsmen”. Remember the time frame and the other prophets that were prophesying during that time. Isaiah shows what that craftsman was doing: “Who hath formed a god, or molten a graven image that is profitable for nothing?” The workmen “are of men”.

The smith works it “with the strength of his arms”. The carpenter “marketh it out with the compass, and maketh it after the figure of a man, according to the beauty of a man; that it may remain in the house.” The craftsman was making idols in the images of men.

He cuts down a tree, and “Then shall it be for a man to burn”; he warms himself and bakes bread with part of it, “yea, he maketh a god, and worshippeth it”. “He burneth part thereof in the fire; with part thereof he eateth flesh”, then “the residue thereof he maketh a god, even his graven image: he falleth down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god.” That is the idol according to their own understanding, profitable for nothing; and they say of them, let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves.
